newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares surge to new records in early trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares surge to new records in early trade.

text.p: German shares surged to yet new record highs on Friday as robust overnight gains on Wall Street and the strong dollar fueled market optimism.
The blue-chip DAX index climbed 52.27 points, or 1.34 percent, in early trade to 3,939.66, pulling within sight of a key psychological target of 4,000.00.
The advance was the latest in a string of gains in German shares which have climbed from 3,795.00 last Friday.
Although the market is expected to stabilise today with U.S. markets closed for the Independence Day holiday, some traders were confident that further gains are around the corner.
"There's no sign that we cannot break 4,000 points in the coming weeks," one trader said, although he noted that investors may be tempted to take profits on the market's recent gains.

Shares in reinsurer Muenchener Rueckversicherungs AG (Munich Re) soared 313 marks to 5,336.00 after announcing overnight it would merge its Hamburg-Mannheimer AG unit with Victoria Holding AG, creating the second largest primary insurance company in Germany.

German utility giant RWE AG was up 65 pfennigs to 77.35 marks after announcing 1996/97 group net profit rose seven percent to just under 1.3 billion marks and that sales climbed to 70.8 billion marks from 65.4 billion marks.
